h1: House for Sale in Faisal Town Islamabad
intro:
Faisal Town Phase 1 / F-18 has an active house-sale market, with current listings across Block A, Block B and Block C.

Buyers should compare houses by block, plot size, construction age, condition, street position, parking, utilities and total transaction cost. Current asking prices vary significantly, so inspect the exact property and verify documents before paying a token.
body:
## Faisal Town Islamabad houses for sale

Faisal Town Phase 1 / F-18 has an established residential resale market with active houses for sale.

Current portal data shows dozens of houses available in Phase 1, with the largest concentration of listings currently appearing in Block C and Block A.

House-sale inventory changes frequently, so this page should be used as a current-market guide rather than a fixed catalogue.

When comparing houses, consider:

- block
- plot size
- bedrooms
- bathrooms
- house age
- construction quality
- finishing
- street and road width
- parking
- utilities
- current occupancy
- asking price
- renovation requirements

The house itself matters as much as the land location.

## Current house prices in Faisal Town F-18

There is no single fixed house price in Faisal Town.

Current asking prices vary according to size, block, construction quality and condition.

Recent market examples include:

- 5-marla houses around PKR 2.6 crore to PKR 2.95 crore
- some premium 5-marla houses asking above PKR 3 crore
- 8-marla houses around PKR 4.1 crore to PKR 4.2 crore in current listings

These figures are seller asking prices and should not be treated as official or guaranteed transaction values.

A brand-new designer house can command considerably more than an older property on the same land size.

## 5 marla houses for sale

5-marla houses are particularly active in the current Faisal Town F-18 market.

Current Phase 1 listings show several 5-marla houses, especially in Block C.

Recent examples include:

- approximately PKR 2.6 crore for a 5-marla double-storey house
- approximately PKR 2.95 crore for a brand-new 5-marla house

Current Block C inventory includes 5-marla houses with layouts such as four bedrooms, multiple bathrooms, two kitchens and double-storey construction. 

When comparing 5-marla houses, check:

- exact plot dimensions
- bedrooms
- double-unit or single-unit layout
- parking
- house age
- finishing
- seepage
- utility connections
- street width
- location within the block

Do not assume all 5-marla houses offer the same usable space.

## 8 marla houses for sale

8-marla houses are another important Faisal Town Phase 1 category.

Current market listings include 30 x 60 houses in Block A and elsewhere in F-18.

Recent asking prices include approximately:

- PKR 4.1 crore for an 8-marla designer house in Block A
- PKR 4.2 crore for another brand-new 8-marla example

Again, these are asking prices, not fixed rates.

An 8-marla buyer should compare:

- 30 x 60 plot dimensions
- bedrooms
- parking
- double-unit potential
- construction age
- street location
- finish quality
- total covered area

## Block A houses for sale

Block A currently has active built-house inventory.

Current Phase 1 portal data shows a meaningful number of house listings in Block A, including 8-marla designer houses.

Block A buyers should check:

- exact street
- road width
- corner or main-road position
- access
- construction quality
- surrounding occupancy
- parking

Because Block A is established, street-level differences can materially affect the value of a house.

## Block B houses for sale

Block B currently has fewer house listings than Block A or Block C, but active inventory still exists.

That means buyers should avoid using one Block B listing as a complete market benchmark.

If considering a Block B house, compare:

- land size
- exact road
- house age
- condition
- bedrooms
- construction quality
- asking price
- nearby comparable properties

Lower listing volume makes current like-for-like comparison more important.

## Block C houses for sale

Block C currently has the strongest visible house inventory among the Phase 1 blocks.

Current portal data shows 24 houses for sale in Block C, including a substantial number of 5-marla properties. :contentReference[oaicite:1]{index=1}

Recent 5-marla examples include asking prices around PKR 2.6 crore and PKR 2.95 crore. :contentReference[oaicite:2]{index=2}

Block C may therefore be particularly useful for buyers comparing smaller ready houses.

## New house vs older house

A brand-new house and an older house should not be compared only by price.

A newer house may offer:

- modern finishing
- newer electrical work
- newer plumbing
- current kitchen design
- updated bathrooms
- lower immediate repair costs

An older house may offer:

- better location
- larger rooms
- mature surroundings
- lower asking price
- stronger structure in some cases

But it may also require substantial renovation.

Compare the total cost after repairs.

## Construction quality checks

Construction quality can materially affect the real value of a house.

Inspect:

- foundations where possible
- visible cracks
- roof condition
- seepage
- dampness
- plumbing
- drainage
- electrical wiring
- switches and sockets
- water tanks
- woodwork
- doors and windows
- tiles and flooring
- kitchen fittings
- bathroom fittings

For a high-value purchase, consider using an independent engineer or experienced construction professional.

## Seepage and water checks

Seepage is one of the most important practical checks in a built house.

Look at:

- basement or ground-floor walls
- bathrooms
- kitchens
- roof
- ceilings
- exterior walls
- water tank area

Fresh paint can sometimes hide old damp patches.

Inspect carefully and, where possible, ask when the house was last painted.

## Electricity, gas and water

Confirm the utility position before purchase.

Check:

- electricity meter
- outstanding electricity bill
- gas connection
- gas bill
- water supply
- water storage
- bore or alternative water arrangement if relevant
- sewerage connection
- internet availability

Do not rely only on the seller saying that “all utilities are available.”

Verify the exact house.

## Parking and street access

A house may look attractive inside but still be less suitable if parking or access is poor.

Check:

- number of cars that fit inside
- gate width
- street width
- ease of turning
- street parking
- traffic
- nearby commercial activity

For larger families, practical access can be as important as the number of bedrooms.

## Owner-occupied, vacant or rented house

Ask whether the property is:

- owner-occupied
- vacant
- rented
- recently completed

If rented, verify:

- tenancy agreement
- tenant notice period
- vacant possession timing
- security deposit held
- rent status

Do not assume immediate vacant possession if a tenant is still occupying the property.

## Documents to verify before buying

Before paying a token, verify the ownership and property details.

The exact documents will depend on the property, but buyers should generally confirm:

- ownership or allotment record
- seller identity
- transfer eligibility
- plot or house number
- dues position
- possession status
- applicable NOC or transfer documentation
- any mortgage or financing issue
- utility bills
- current occupancy

The paperwork should match the property you physically inspected.

## Token payment checks

Before paying a token:

1. Verify seller identity.
2. Confirm ownership or authority to sell.
3. Confirm exact house and plot number.
4. Agree the total sale price.
5. Record the token amount.
6. Record whether the token is refundable.
7. Record the remaining payment schedule.
8. Record fixtures included in the sale.
9. Confirm vacant possession timing.
10. Obtain a written receipt.

Avoid paying a substantial token based only on photographs or a portal advertisement.

## Fixtures included in the sale

Clarify which fixtures and fittings remain with the house.

Possible items include:

- air conditioners
- solar system
- geysers
- ceiling fans
- kitchen appliances
- wardrobes
- curtains
- CCTV system
- water pumps
- UPS or batteries

List significant included items in writing.

## Total transaction cost

The asking price is not the complete purchase cost.

Also consider:

- transfer charges
- applicable taxes
- agent commission
- legal/document review cost
- outstanding dues
- repairs
- renovation
- utility arrears
- moving cost

A lower-priced house requiring major renovation may ultimately cost more than a better-finished property.

## How to compare two houses

Use the same criteria for every shortlisted property:

1. Block
2. Plot size
3. Asking price
4. Bedrooms
5. Bathrooms
6. Construction age
7. Condition
8. Parking
9. Street width
10. Utilities
11. Documents
12. Renovation cost
13. Total transaction cost

This creates a much more useful comparison than choosing only from photos.

## House vs plot in Faisal Town

A ready house may suit buyers who want to move in quickly.

A plot may suit buyers who want:

- their own design
- construction control
- staged construction spending
- future flexibility

When comparing a house with a plot, separate:

- land value
- construction value
- expected repair cost
- new construction cost

A ready house premium only makes sense if the building itself adds genuine value.

## House for sale vs house for rent

If you are unsure whether to buy or rent, compare the expected holding period.

Buying may make more sense for someone planning to stay long term and able to manage the upfront cost.

Renting may suit someone who:

- needs flexibility
- is testing the area
- expects to relocate
- does not want immediate capital commitment

Use the separate Faisal Town rental guide for current rent checks.

## Before making a final offer

Before final negotiation:

- visit during daylight
- inspect the roof
- test water pressure
- check electrical points
- inspect seepage
- inspect parking
- verify the street
- check documents
- compare current nearby listings
- calculate repairs
- confirm possession date

The strongest buying decision combines the location, house condition and documentation rather than focusing on only one of them.
